findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: entire program aborts with panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string) is embedded inside load_metrics, which is the only entry point. I/O is fused with parsing and domain construction.
findings.failure_mode: shell and domain concerns are inseparable; cannot reuse parsing logic without file system access; pure tests require real files
findings.fix: split into shell fn load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that calls domain fn parse_records(records: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; read file in shell, pass lines to pure parser

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs stdout I/O inside parsing logic. Domain parsing must be pure.
findings.failure_mode: parser has observable side-effects, breaks determinism, contaminates pure computation with shell concerns, and produces noisy output in tests
findings.fix: remove println!; move all logging to the shell layer after parse results are produced

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses index 0 with no bounds check; empty or malformed lines cause panic
findings.failure_mode: a single blank or short line in the input file causes a panic via index-out-of-bounds

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index 1 with no bounds check; lines with one field cause panic
findings.failure_mode: a line missing the value field (e.g. trailing newline or malformed entry) panics on index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or require exactly two fields

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics when the value field is not a valid u32 string
findings.failure_mode: any non-numeric value in the data file aborts the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid("value")) and return Result from map closure

findings.problem: (parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16) is a lossy cast from u32 to u16; values 65536+ silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value outside u16 range wraps around silently, producing an incorrect Record with a corrupted value field
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow("value")) or parse directly to u16 with parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(...)

findings.problem: The entire function from line 8-22 fuses file I/O, stdout logging, error-prone string splitting, and domain construction into a single fn. No pure parsing boundary exists.
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic in isolation; every test requires filesystem setup; shell failures mask domain logic bugs
findings.fix: extract a pure fn parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that consumes trusted input; keep load_metrics as the thin shell that reads the file and delegates

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> with no capacity cap. No max_items parameter, no try_reserve, no outer bound on iteration count.
findings.failure_mode: an adversarial or unbounded input file causes uncontrolled heap allocation, potentially OOM-crashing the process
findings.fix: add max_items: usize parameter; call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?; enforce count <= max_items before push; reject excess with ParseError::TooMany

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type. All failures (IO, parse, bounds) surface as panics via unwrap().
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from value overflow; cannot implement recovery or user-visible error messages
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Allocation, Invalid(&'static str), Overflow(&'static str) }; return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: Raw string from file is split on ',' and individual fields are indexed and parsed without a fallible smart constructor. Hostile inputs reach the domain directly.
findings.failure_mode: empty strings, extra commas, whitespace-only fields, and non-numeric values all construct invalid Records instead of being rejected at the boundary
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; let (_name, value_str) = ...; parse value_str with validated conversion; wrap name in a validated newtype

findings.problem: Record { name: String, value: u16 } stores raw primitives. No newtypes, no invariants, no smart constructor. Any code can construct an invalid Record.
findings.failure_mode: illegal domain states are representable; a name field could be empty or whitespace; value could exceed domain constraints without explicit checks
findings.fix: use newtypes: struct Name(String) with a smart constructor rejecting empty/whitespace; struct Value(u16) if domain has additional constraints; Record { name: Name, value: Value } with a private constructor

findings.problem: use std::fs imports the fs module but the crate has no explicit re-export strategy. The bare use pollutes the public API surface.
findings.failure_mode: consumers of this library may import std::fs through the public interface, creating coupling and breaking encapsulation
findings.fix: remove bare use std::fs; use it locally inside the function or module scope; do not re-export std modules publicly

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() splits into all parts and collects into Vec<String>, then indexes by position. For a known two-field CSV line, split_once is the correct approach.
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec<String> for every line (intermediate allocation), iterates all fields when only two are needed, and loses the invariant that each line has exactly two fields
findings.fix: let (name_str, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; parse name_str and value_str directly

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics. No baseline or measured bottleneck is identified.
findings.failure_mode: any performance optimization claim is ungrounded; the intermediate Vec<String> allocations per line and the println! call are unmeasured hot spots
findings.fix: add a benchmark with workload (file size, line count), baseline measurements, new implementation comparison, and target hardware specification

findings.problem: Record fields are pub, allowing external mutation of domain values after construction.
findings.failure_mode: domain invariants can be violated after construction by directly mutating name or value fields
findings.fix: make Record fields private with getter methods, or derive Copy/Clone and use builder pattern for construction

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics performance
no profiler data identifying measured bottleneck
no allocation evidence (no try_reserve, no capacity bounds)
no second-ring evidence (no integration tests exercising full I/O path)
no command evidence (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test were not run)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has 13 findings including 10 blockers: unwrap panic surfaces on every error path, hidden file I/O and stdout logging fused with parsing, unchecked indexing on split results, a lossy u32-to-u16 cast, no typed error taxonomy, no bounded allocation, no pure parsing boundary, raw primitive domain fields, and no performance evidence. Every unwrap and unchecked index is a guaranteed panic on hostile input. The code must be restructured into a shell/domain split with Result return types, bounded allocation with try_reserve, checked conversions, and removed side-effects before this crate can be considered safe.
